title: Is Your Website Showing in Google’s AI Answers? A Guide to the New Search Console Reports
content:
As Google’s search results keep changing, a website’s visibility is no longer limited to the traditional blue links users are used to seeing on the results page.

Today, Google shows AI-powered answers through features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode. These features change how users reach information, and with it, how website performance in search is measured.

That is why Google has started testing new reports in Google Search Console called:

Search Generative AI Performance Reports

These reports are designed to help website owners understand how often their pages appear in AI features across Search and Discover. The update is currently available to a limited number of websites and is expected to roll out more widely after the testing and feedback phase.

In this SEO House article, we explain what these reports are, what data they show, why they do not show clicks yet, and how website owners can respond to this new shift in SEO.

1. What are Search Generative AI Performance Reports?

Search Generative AI Performance Reports are new reports in Google Search Console that measure how often a website’s pages appear in AI-powered search features.

Put simply:
Instead of tracking only how your website appears in traditional search results, you will start to see whether your pages appear in Google’s new experiences, such as:

  • AI Overviews
  • AI Mode
  • AI features in Google Discover

This matters because Google no longer always presents results in the same old format. For some searches, users get a concise, source-backed answer, and your website may appear inside that answer even if the user never interacts with the result the way they would in traditional search.

2. Why does this update matter to website owners?

Until now, SEO performance analysis has relied mainly on metrics such as:

  • Keyword rankings.
  • Impressions in search results.
  • Clicks.
  • Click-through rate (CTR).
  • The pages that attract the most traffic.

But as AI becomes part of the search experience, a new kind of presence has emerged, which we can call:

AI Visibility

In other words, a website’s ability to appear in Google’s AI-powered answers, not just in the traditional links.

And this is where the competition changes.

A website is no longer competing only for a link position on the first page; it is also competing to be a source Google trusts when it builds an AI answer for the user.

3. What data do the new reports show?

According to Google’s announcement, the new reports do not offer all the data website owners are used to in the standard Performance report, but they do provide important metrics for understanding visibility in AI features.

This data can help SEO teams see which types of content are appearing in AI features, and whether that visibility comes from educational articles, service pages, product pages or long-form informational content.

4. The key point: the reports do not show click data

As useful as these reports are, there is one point you need to keep in mind:

The reports do not yet show the number of clicks coming from AI features.

This means a website owner may know that a certain page appeared in an AI Overview or in AI Mode, but will not know exactly how many users clicked the link from within that experience.

That leaves the analysis incomplete.

Visibility matters, but on its own it is not enough to evaluate a website’s business or marketing performance. What matters most is always understanding whether that visibility leads to visits, engagement, inquiries or sales.

Google has said it is still working with website owners to understand which metrics are most useful and may add more metrics later.

5. Will these reports be available for every website?

No, not at the moment.

Google has explained that the reports are rolling out gradually to a limited number of website owners for testing and feedback before a wider rollout.

If the report does not appear in your Search Console account, the reason may be one of the following:

  • The report has not reached your website yet.
  • Your website has not received enough impressions in AI features.
  • Your website is not eligible for, or is excluded from, appearing in these features.
  • The feature is still in limited testing.

So if you cannot see the report right now, that does not necessarily mean there is a problem with your website.

6. A new option: opting out of AI responses

Alongside the new reports, Google has also started testing an option in Search Console that lets some website owners prevent their content from appearing in AI features, such as:

  • AI Overviews
  • AI Mode
  • AI Overviews in Discover

This option gives website owners more control over how their content is used in AI answers.

But the decision is not a simple one.

Google has made clear that websites choosing not to appear in these features will not receive traffic or impressions from them. At the same time, it has confirmed that this choice is not used as a ranking signal in traditional search results outside AI features.

In other words:
You can stop your website from appearing in AI features, but that does not mean your rankings in regular search results will be directly affected by that decision.

7. Should you block your website from appearing in AI results?

There is no single answer for every website.

Before deciding, ask yourself:

  • Does appearing in AI answers help build users’ trust in your brand?
  • Is your website’s name or link clearly visible in the answers?
  • Does this visibility raise awareness of your website even without clicks?
  • Does your content model depend on direct visits and advertising?
  • Does answering the question inside Google reduce the chances of users visiting your website?

For some websites, especially news sites or those that rely on ad-driven traffic, the decision may be more sensitive.

For service businesses, companies, online stores and websites building long-term content authority, appearing in AI features can be an important opportunity to strengthen trust and digital presence.

8. How can you analyze AI visibility in practice?

Even without click data, website owners can get value from the new reports, once available, in several ways:

First: Identify the pages that appear in AI features

If certain pages appear repeatedly in the AI reports, that is a sign Google sees them as useful sources.

This is where you should analyze:

  • The page type.
  • The content format.
  • The depth of the answer.
  • Whether clear data is present.
  • How the headings are organized.
  • Whether there are questions and answers.
  • How closely the content matches user intent.

Second: Compare AI visibility with traditional traffic

You may notice that a certain page gets impressions in AI features but does not get a proportional amount of traffic.

This does not necessarily mean the page is weak; it may mean Google is using its content to build a direct answer for the user.

Third: Review countries and devices

Knowing which countries your visibility comes from helps you understand which markets Google considers your website relevant to.

Device data can show whether visibility happens more on mobile or desktop, which matters for improving page experience, speed and content layout.

Fourth: Monitor changes over time

Because the reports show data over time, an SEO team can track how content updates, page improvements or Google updates affect the website’s visibility in AI features.

9. What kind of content is best positioned to appear in AI answers?

There is no guaranteed formula, but based on how search is evolving, the content most likely to appear in AI answers is usually content that:

  • Answers a clear question.
  • Is organized under logical headings.
  • Gives direct explanations, not filler.
  • Contains real expertise or practical examples.
  • Covers the topic in sufficient depth.
  • Clarifies definitions, differences and tables where needed.
  • Connects user intent with an actual solution.
  • Reflects the website’s expertise in its field.

So simply writing a long article is no longer enough.
What matters is that the article is useful, clear, trustworthy and easy to understand, for users and search engines alike.

10. How can websites prepare for this stage?

At SEO House, we believe the approach to AI search should not start with gaming the technology, but with improving content quality and building real authority in your field.

To prepare for this stage, we recommend focusing on the following:

1. Build specialized content, not generic content

Generic content that repeats the same information found on dozens of other websites will not be enough.

Your website should offer a clear angle, hands-on experience, examples and details that help Google understand why this content deserves to appear.

2. Structure content so it is easy to understand

Using subheadings, tables, FAQs and a logical structure helps both users and search engines understand the page better.

3. Optimize your key pages, not just articles

AI visibility is not limited to articles.
Service pages, product pages, category pages and FAQ pages can also qualify to appear if they are well organized and useful.

4. Strengthen trust signals

Your website should clearly show what supports trust, such as:

  • Clear information about the company.
  • Team expertise.
  • Case studies.
  • Customer reviews.
  • Accurate service pages.
  • Content that shows the website’s real specialization.

5. Monitor Search Console regularly

When the new reports appear in your account, do not treat them as side numbers; treat them as part of measuring your website’s overall performance.

11. Traditional SEO vs. AI visibility

12. What does this update mean for the future of SEO?

This update does not mean traditional SEO is over.

But it does confirm that measuring success in search has become broader than ranking for a keyword or increasing traffic.

In the coming period, website owners will need to think about two questions at once:

Is my website showing in search results?
and
Is my content appearing in Google’s AI-powered answers?

The difference between the two questions matters.

A website may be present in traditional results but completely absent from AI Overviews.
The opposite can also happen: a page appears inside an AI answer but does not generate clear, trackable clicks.

This is where SEO becomes more strategic, because it is no longer just about optimizing a page; it is about building a trusted presence for your website across the entire search ecosystem.

13. A quick checklist for website owners

If you run a website or an online store, start by reviewing these points:

  • Watch for the Generative AI reports in Search Console once they become available.
  • Identify the pages that appear in AI features.
  • Review the content quality of the pages that are getting visibility.
  • Compare AI visibility with traditional organic traffic.
  • Do not decide to opt out of AI features without a clear analysis.
  • Optimize your service and product pages with the same care you give your articles.
  • Use clear headings and direct questions in your content.
  • Add examples, tables and practical details that build trust.
  • Monitor how content updates affect your visibility over time.
  • Treat AI visibility as part of your SEO strategy, not as a separate number.

Conclusion: The next competition is not just for the top link

Launching dedicated reports in Search Console for how websites appear in AI features is more than a technical update.

It is a clear sign that Google is reshaping how websites appear, and how that visibility is measured.

In the past, the most important question was:
Is your website on the first page?

Now, the question is starting to become:
Is your website’s content good enough to be part of Google’s own answer?

At SEO House, we believe the next stage of search engine optimization will be built on trustworthy, well-structured, specialized content, not just content that targets keywords.

Appearing in search results matters.
But appearing in AI answers may become one of the most important arenas of SEO competition in the period ahead.

seo.rank_math_description: What Google’s new Search Console AI reports show, why they lack click data, and how to measure and improve your website’s visibility in AI Overviews.
